gen-fs-styro-gf-anek-gujarati: Anek Gujarati reads wide and friendly, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals and a c that gapes open. Styro, crowded and retro, is its tightly shut opposite.
gen-fs-styro-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Tight and loud up top, loose below. Anek Gurmukhi keeps big open counters and generous round curves in its sans lowercase, so a long passage moves along without any crowding.
gen-fs-styro-gf-anek-kannada: Anek Kannada reads modern and upright, its high x-height recalling a squared-off woodblock letter, with terminals that stop well short of the stem. And over a long passage it stays open and easy, a sharp foil to Styro's crowded retro headings.
gen-fs-styro-gf-anek-malayalam: Anek Malayalam reads like a plain sans with almost no step between lowercase and caps, and curve tips that never quite touch. But Styro, big and short, is where the heading earns its keep.
gen-fs-styro-gf-anek-odia: Styro brings a retro, commanding crowd of letters, pressed together with barely any gap in its e and c shapes. Anek Odia answers with unsealed rounds like an unlatched hook, a plain sans loosening everything.
gen-fs-styro-gf-anek-tamil: Styro is retro and commanding, with letters packed tight. Anek Tamil, a plain sans, then opens things up with big round bowls and c and s shapes that look half unwrapped.
gen-fs-styro-gf-anek-telugu: Anek Telugu sets a reading rhythm of wide, tall bowls, with rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook. Over a long passage it feels friendly and unhurried, nothing like Styro's crush.
gen-fs-styro-gf-anuphan: Styro presses its letters shut, retro and crowded, with e and c shapes barely gapped. It does the commanding; Anuphan, a sans of big round bowls and open curves, does the easy reading.
gen-fs-styro-gf-arimo: Styro crowds its retro letters together, closing the gaps in its e and c shapes. Arimo then reads with a tall mean line and spacious terminal gaps, so a long passage never feels cramped.
gen-fs-styro-gf-armata: Crowded retro punch meets breathing room. And Armata, a sans-serif with spacious gaps in its rounds and lowercase filling most of the letter height, loosens everything Styro squeezes shut.
